name: cyber-aware-creations
description: Twelve NIST-aligned skills for security leaders, running locally against your own files. Nine own data and persist it: risk-register scores and tracks a cybersecurity risk register with change history and board dashboards; nist-csf assesses your programme against NIST CSF 2.0 as a tracked Organizational Profile with gap analysis, coverage reporting and read-only crosswalks to ISO 27001, CIS Controls and 800-53; metrics-register trends security metrics and KRIs with direction-aware thresholds; exceptions-register runs the lifecycle of accepted risks and control exceptions and exports the evidence artifact an auditor asks for; incident-materiality structures an SEC Item 1.05 and DORA disclosure determination and its clocks, and never emits a verdict; business-context records the organisation's own facts — revenue base, crown jewels, board-voiced tolerance — and the applicability profile that narrows what a consuming skill asks — every register reads it — risk, posture, metrics, exceptions and incident. vendor-register keeps third-party arrangements with a criticality derived by tracing what each one supports back to a business workflow and confirmed by a named person, and emits no vendor score. ai-register keeps a security inventory of the AI the organisation runs — risk lives in the deployment, not the model — deriving what each deployment is exposed to under the NIST adversarial machine learning taxonomy from its recorded attributes, recording controls with evidence and a date, and never marking an attack class handled, because those mitigations are empirical and published defences have repeatedly been broken. attention-surface is the weekly counterpart to board-pack: it reads the escalations every producer already computes, groups them by decision rather than by producer, orders them without a score, and shows what changed since the last review — owning no data, muting nothing, and reporting a register it could not read as unread rather than as clean. ciso-board-translation owns the board-facing language they all call, with sourced regulatory receipts. policy-register keeps the register of security policies an auditor asks for — what exists, who owns it, what version, who approved it on what date, when it is next reviewed, and which requirement each document is aimed at — grounded in the Policy and Procedures control of every SP 800-53 Rev. 5 family and in CSF 2.0 GV.PO, and it refuses to say a requirement is met, covered or compliant because a policy maps to it: a mapping records that a document exists and what it is aimed at, nothing more. It supersedes and never deletes, because the audit question is what was in force on the date of the incident. board-pack assembles the quarterly pack as a print-ready document and an editable PowerPoint deck, and owns no data at all.
